sections.description: Prophecies of judgment against neighboring nations and Israel for their sins

sections.title: Accusations Against Israel
sections.description: Prophetic accusations against Israel's injustice and pride

sections.description: Five visions concerning God's judgment and the conflict with priest Amaziah

sections.description: The promise to restore David's fallen tent

events.title: Amos' Call and Introduction
events.description: Amos, a shepherd from Tekoa in Judah, receives God's word about Israel. He prophesied during the reigns of Uzziah king of Judah and Jeroboam II king of Israel, two years before the earthquake. The Lord speaks from Zion, and the pastures dry up.

events.title: Judgment Against the Neighboring Nations
events.description: God proclaims judgment against Damascus, Gaza, Tyre, Edom, Ammon, and Moab for their atrocities. Each oracle begins with the formula "For three transgressions and for four". These nations have committed war crimes, slavery, and broken covenant relationships.

events.title: Judgment Against Judah and Israel
events.description: After judging the neighboring nations, Amos turns to Judah for rejecting the Lord's law, and then to Israel. Israel is accused of selling the righteous for silver and the poor for a pair of sandals. They oppress the weak, profane God's holy name, and drink wine from fines in their gods' houses.

events.title: "You only have I known"
events.description: God reminds Israel of their unique position as His chosen people. But this privilege carries greater responsibility: "You only have I known among all the families of the earth; therefore I will punish you for all your sins." Amos explains that the prophet speaks because the Lord has spoken, and warns of the destruction of Samaria.

events.title: "Accusation against the wealthy women of Samaria"
events.description: Amos addresses the affluent women of Samaria as "cows of Bashan" because they oppress the poor and crush the needy, while demanding that their husbands provide them with wine. God swears by His holiness that they will be led away with hooks and fishhooks.

events.title: "Seek me, and you shall live"
events.description: Amos sings a lament over Israel and calls the people to repentance. The famous verse reads: "Let justice roll down like waters, and righteousness like an ever-flowing stream." God rejects their religious festivals and sacrifices because they lack justice and mercy.

events.title: "Woe to the complacent in Zion"
events.description: Amos cries woe over those who live in luxury and self-assurance in Zion and on the mountains of Samaria. They lie on ivory beds, eat the finest lambs, sing to the sound of the harp, and anoint themselves with fine oil, yet do not grieve over the ruin of Joseph. Therefore, they shall be led away as the first among the captives.

events.title: "The vision of locusts and fire"
events.description: In the first two visions, God shows Amos a swarm of locusts devouring the land and a fire consuming the great deep. Both times, Amos intercedes for the people, saying: "Lord God, forgive! How can Jacob stand? He is so small." And the Lord relents and says: "This shall not happen."

events.title: "The vision of the plumb line"
events.description: In the third vision, Amos sees the Lord standing by a wall with a plumb line in His hand. The plumb line symbolizes God's righteous standard by which He measures the people. This time, God says: "I will no longer pass over them." Israel's high places shall be destroyed, and God will rise against the house of Jeroboam with the sword.

events.title: "The conflict with priest Amaziah"
events.description: Amaziah, the priest at Bethel, sends word to King Jeroboam, accusing Amos of conspiracy. He orders Amos to flee back to Judah and prophesy there. Amos replies that he is neither a prophet nor a prophet's son, but a shepherd and a tender of sycamore figs, whom the Lord took from the flock and sent to prophesy against Israel.

events.title: The Vision of the Basket of Ripe Fruit
events.description: In the fourth vision, God shows Amos a basket of ripe summer fruit. Through a play on words (qayits/qets), God says that the end has come for Israel. Amos condemns those who cheat the poor, tamper with weights and measures, and make the Sabbath a burden. God swears that he will never forget their deeds.

events.title: The Vision of the Lord at the Altar
events.description: In the fifth and final vision of judgment, Amos sees the Lord standing by the altar and commanding that the temple be torn down over the heads of the people. No one shall escape, neither to the realm of the dead nor up into heaven. God's eyes are fixed on the sinful kingdom to destroy it from the face of the earth.

events.title: The Promise of David's Fallen Hut
events.description: The book ends with a message of hope. God promises to raise up again David's fallen hut and restore his people. The mountains shall drip with wine, and Israel will be planted in their own land and never again be uprooted. This promise is cited by James in Acts as fulfilled through Christ.
